97bceaeb6c7f0156ddcd1353c91d2ddc86adc942.summary: enSilo reports new activity it believes is by Chinese cyber espionage group APT10, detected in April 2019 and surfacing in Southeast Asia. Two loader variants abuse the legitimate Java executable jjs.exe to sideload a DLL and inject a decrypted payload into svchost.exe. Payloads include PlugX and a modified Quasar RAT with SharpSploit. The samples originated from the Philippines, and the report links the infrastructure to APT10's history, including servers in South Korea.

972b5646b64f08b58a794e17796900da4401e4b2.summary: Kaspersky Lab's GReAT team reports on Skimer, malware that infects ATMs and activates only when a specific magic card is inserted. Kaspersky has identified 49 modifications, 37 of them targeting ATMs from one manufacturer, and the most recent was found in May 2016. The report calls the investigation ongoing and recommends ATM hardening and checks on card data.

97a0c44d6f4a01a71939fff15a41e8a67d2d3a22.summary: Coveware blog post (27 January 2022) on the evolution of ransomware-as-a-service (RaaS), framed as an innovation adoption curve. It covers early TOR payment sites (Locky, 2016), GandCrab's per-machine keys and MSP attacks, Maze's data-theft extortion, and the Russian FSB arrests of REvil operators in 2020 onward. It reports backup viability rising to 42% of victims in 2021, more data-leak extortion, re-extortion and premature leaks mostly by RaaS actors, and a REvil backdoor that let its administrators scam affiliates. It also notes FIN7 trying to recruit IT staff under the guise of…

hedges: The report says the 2020-2021 backup trend is 'surely influenced by multiple variables', so it does not establish a single cause.
The report says it 'may deduce' that threat actors rely less on encrypted backups and more on the threat of data leakage.
The report 'infer[s]' that Closed RaaS vetting has deteriorated and/or actors value reputation less, and does not settle which.
The report describes Closed RaaS groups as 'theoretically' more experienced and selective than other groups.
The FIN7 fake-firm recruitment is reported by security researchers, and the report quotes Gemini's belief that it is an attempt to hire cheap labor.
The REvil backdoor claim is relayed from Yelisey Boguslavskiy of Advanced Intelligence as reported by the report; the report does not independently verify it.
The 2021 figures are described as a year-to-date examination of Coveware's own 2021 attack data.
